headline: Monitor Snowmelt for Highway and Hydrothermal Access
reservation: While day-use entry does not currently require a timed reservation, all park campgrounds require advance booking through official channels. The narrow window of July through September sees high demand; seasonal snow impacts the opening of Lassen Park Highway and Bumpass Hell boardwalk. Check the official NPS site for current status before travel.

days.title: Hydrothermal Wonders and Alpine Vistas

stops.name: Bumpass Hell
stops.detail: Walk the three-mile round-trip trail to see boiling mud pots and turquoise pools from the safety of the official boardwalk.

stops.name: Lassen Peak
stops.detail: Climb the five-mile round-trip trail for a strenuous ascent to the summit of one of the world's largest plug dome volcanoes.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the 30-mile Lassen Park Highway; conditions vary significantly with weather.
days.note: Stay on designated boardwalks to avoid unstable, scalding geothermal ground.

days.title: Reflective Lakes and Volcanic History

stops.name: Manzanita Lake
stops.detail: Walk the gentle 1.5-mile loop for views of Lassen Peak reflected in the water or engage in non-motorized boating.

stops.name: Devastated Area
stops.detail: Explore the interpretive trail showcasing the path and massive boulders left by the 1915 eruption.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for local transfers between north entrance sites.
days.note: Water temperatures remain low; use caution during lake activities.

days.title: Remote Cones and Painted Sands

stops.name: Cinder Cone
stops.detail: Hike the steep volcanic scoria for views of the crater and the surrounding Fantastic Lava Beds.

stops.name: Painted Dunes
stops.detail: Observe the vibrant red and orange oxidized volcanic ash hills from the rim of Cinder Cone.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for travel to the Butte Lake area; includes unpaved sections.
days.note: The Cinder Cone ascent involves loose volcanic gravel; pace yourself accordingly.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Lassen Peak and Bumpass Hell lots frequently reach capacity by mid-morning in peak summer. Early arrival is suggested to secure access to these popular trailheads.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable throughout the park interior and high-elevation passes. Download navigation and trail maps before departing Redding or Chester.

intel.title: Regional Services
intel.text: Fuel is typically unavailable within park boundaries during the off-season. Confirm status at Shingletown or Chester before entering the volcanic corridor.

intel.title: Highway Seasonality
intel.text: The main park highway often remains closed due to snow until late June or early July. Check the official park road status for through-access updates.

intel.title: Thermal Safety
intel.text: Hydrothermal areas like Sulphur Works are easily reached from the road but require strict adherence to barriers. Thin crusts near steam vents pose severe burn risks.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at Redding Municipal Airport, secure supplies in Redding, and proceed to the Manzanita Lake or Kohm Yah-mah-nee gateway.
plan.vehicle: Check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved roads like the route to Butte Lake; 4WD is advised for early spring transitions.
plan.goldenHour: Manzanita Lake Shoreline, subject to clear skies and seasonal cloud cover.
